# 後藤梨春『本草綱目補物品目録』 — THE EARLIEST JAPANESE RECORD OF THE TOMATO
# NDL pid 2556504, Public Domain Mark, 51 canvases, manuscript (写), undated.
# Text quoted from the NDL full-text (OCR) index, 2026-08-31. NO SCAN IS HELD.

珊瑚樹茄 高尺許 葉似艾葉而大 毎葉小片両々相對
実似酸醬而大 無殻苞 生青熟赤 一名唐柿

"Sangoju-nasu (coral-tree aubergine). About a foot high. LEAVES LIKE MUGWORT
(ai) BUT LARGER, each leaf with small leaflets in opposing pairs. FRUIT LIKE A
PHYSALIS (sankashō) BUT LARGER, WITHOUT A HUSK, green when young, red when
ripe. Also called togaki."

WHY THIS IS THE TOMATO, AND NOT A HUSK-CHERRY:
葉似艾 — "leaves like mugwort" is the same diagnostic the Chinese Qunfang Pu
uses for 蕃柿 (see the 1708/1725/1728 sources in evidence/).
無殻苞 — "WITHOUT A HUSK" is precisely what separates a tomato from Physalis,
and the entry makes the comparison explicitly in order to deny it.
生青熟赤 — green then red.

WHY IT MATTERS: Shirai Mitsutarō, Shokubutsu torai kō, names THIS WORK as the
first Japanese book to record the tomato. Gotō Rishun lived 1696-1771, so this
PREDATES Seikei zusetsu (1804), in which this project recorded a Japanese negative.

*** THE DATE IS NOT ESTABLISHED. DO NOT PUBLISH ONE. ***
To date it, use Shirai's own chronology 『日本博物学年表』(1891), NDL pid 993896.
